newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed slighty higher in holiday-sapped trading, but prices were marked down late in the day after a sell-off in other markets.
Most of the gains, registered on the opening to reflect the strength in U.S. Treasuries the previous night, slipped away as U.S. Treasuries and Bund futures succumbed to profit taking.
Dealers said volumes were low in pre-weekend trading marred also by the absence from the market of key players after the Ascension Day holiday on Thursday.
"You saw how easily it comes off," one dealer said of the sell-off.
One dealer said Dutch institutions were still absent from the guilder market, waiting for lower levels to invest.
He said they may be hoping for Bund futures to dip to 101.00 before wading back into state loans.
Dealers saw U.S. economic data next week as crucial for the direction of guilder yields. "Sentiment has been more positive in last few weeks," one added.
He said Dutch players were also awaiting the new tap issue on May 27, with a reopening of the 5.75 pct February 2007 bond favoured.
